title: Conditional Security Checklist Proxy & Crediting Pilot for Enterprise Contracts
creator: Jordan Li
description: Run a 6-week pilot that automatically answers low-risk portions of SIG/CAIQ and similar security questionnaires using a 'checklist proxy' built from existing platform artifacts (docs, config, telemetry). When customers accept the proxy answers, apply a conditional pricing credit that reduces Sales/SE manual labor cost in the onboarding contract. The pilot should validate accuracy, surface a minimal manual review workflow for flagged items, and provide an auditable evidence bundle for legal and procurement reviews.
acceptance_criteria: Proxy can auto-fill >=70% of SIG/CAIQ items for low-complexity requests with data-backed evidence links
System generates an evidence bundle (docs + signed metadata) for every auto-filled answer
Manual reviewer flow handles flagged items with SLA <= 48 hours for enterprise customers
Crediting engine issues a one-time onboarding credit when the customer accepts the proxy answers, visible on the quote and billing dashboard
Telemetry captures precision/recall of auto-answers and customer acceptance rate (target >= 60% acceptance)
tasks: Map SIG/CAIQ question taxonomy to platform evidence sources (runtime configs, KMS attestations, SOC artifacts)
Prototype a lightweight Checklist Proxy service and API to fetch canonical answers and evidence URIs
Design UI flow in Console for customer acceptance and 'request manual review' button
Implement a Crediting Rule that ties acceptance event to a pilot pricing offset for quotes
Create audit/export format for evidence bundle and store in compliance S3 bucket with retention metadata
Run a 4-customer closed pilot and collect metrics and qualitative feedback
comments: 2026-02-11 - Jordan Li: Kickoff with Security, Legal, Sales Engineering. Agreement to only auto-answer low-risk controls (data residency, encryption at rest, basic auth configs). Legal insists on signed metadata for any auto-attestations.
2026-02-16 - Emily Chen (Security): Prototype evidence mapping looks promising for 80 control IDs. Remaining ~200 controls are high-context and will be surfaced to SEs.

2026-02-20 - Miguel Santos (Sales Eng): Sales concern: credits must be visible in quote PDF and in Salesforce to avoid manual reconciliation. Action: integrate credit memo with billing and SF opportunity.

2026-02-24 - Design review (Aisha Patel): Proposed console mockups show customer-facing checklist with green/amber/red states. Designer requests explicit wording for 'auto-filled' vs 'submitted by SE' to avoid misleading customers.

2026-02-27 - Priya Menon: Implemented initial Checklist Proxy API (internal PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/checklist-proxy/pull/42). Added evidence bundle generator. Next: wiring crediting rule and console acceptance flow.

2026-03-01 - Legal note (Rebecca Alvarez): Approved pilot scope with constraints: auto-answers must include evidence URIs and a legal disclaimer; credits cannot be greater than 10% of first-year contract value without explicit Legal approval. Marking security_review_required = true.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive automation reduces SE load but increases legal exposure. Mitigation: conservative scope + evidence + human-in-loop for medium/high risk controls.
Fallbacks: if proxy accuracy <55% in pilot, revert to 'assistive' mode where proxy suggestions are flagged but not auto-applied to contract credits.
Billing integration complexity: current billing system cannot apply ad-hoc credits for hosted trials; requires a small billing API extension (tracked as engineering spike).
Success metrics: time-to-close reduction, SE hours saved per onboarding, customer satisfaction with security intake, fraction of questions auto-answered and accepted
